issues: Integrity: no problems found. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. All randomness comes from the seeded rng, and the existing repair step still makes the packing valid.

Design weakness, not a bug: every restart uses the same 32 Halton points, moved together by one random 2-D shift (mod 1). Restarts differ in only 2 random values, where uniform starts differ in 64. That likely explains the drop from -2.9334 to -2.9307. The result is still meaningful.

Recomputed z: the sd of the difference is 0.0034*sqrt(1/1+1/1) = 0.00481. The difference (incumbent loss minus candidate loss) is -2.9334 - (-2.9307) = -0.0027, so z = -0.0027/0.00481 = -0.56. This matches the reported -0.566 up to rounding of the shown values. The candidate is slightly worse and well within noise.
Each side has only 1 run, so the evidence is weak either way. Rejecting is consistent with the numbers, and no claims in the diff contradict them.
